seed: A layer name longer than the timing strip's name column. Two layers called settings-capture-top and settings-capture-left, each given the same rotation, so the strip holds two headings that begin the same way and differ only at the end. At Next defaults, nothing switched on by hand. The strip has to tell the two apart on sight, and a name it cannot show whole has to be readable in full by resting the pointer on it, without leaving the strip.

steps.note: three headings on the strip. The two long ones begin the same way and differ only at the end, and the cut keeps the end: one reads as the top one, the other as the left one. The short Rectangle sits in the column whole, exactly as before. Each heading starts with the mark for its kind, the way the Make a bell swing mock draws it: a square for the two rectangles, a circle for the ellipse.
resting on the cut heading raises the app's own tooltip carrying the whole name, settings-capture-top, just over the heading, without leaving the strip.
and the other one says settings-capture-left, so the two are told apart in full.
the same name, raised the way a hand raises it: the pointer resting on the face of the cut heading, settin…re-top, brings up settings-capture-top.
resting on the Rectangle heading, which fits the column whole, raises nothing: a tooltip that only repeats what is already on screen is noise.
